title: 3rd Stopping Place 4th Truth 2 Kinds Of Provision

questions.question: What is the second kind of provision described in the passage?
questions.answer: It is the kind people treat like a need because of habits, waste, and wrong use, even though it is not a real basic need.

questions.question: Is this second kind of provision always promised to every person?
questions.answer: No. It is not guaranteed. Allah may give it, and He may withhold it.

questions.question: What good attitude should a person have when seeking this second kind of provision?
questions.answer: A person should live simply, be content, work in a halal way, and see that effort as worship and a du‘a through action.

questions.question: How does a thankful person live, according to the passage?
questions.answer: That person receives Allah’s gifts with thanks and lives in a peaceful and pleasant way.

questions.question: What bad things happen to a person who follows wastefulness and greed?
questions.answer: Such a person leaves lawful effort, keeps chasing after people, lives lazily and wrongly, and makes life miserable for himself.

questions.question: Besides the stomach, what other parts of a person need provision?
questions.answer: The inner and outer abilities also need it, like the heart, spirit, mind, eyes, ears, and mouth.

questions.question: Who gives provision to these human abilities?
questions.answer: Allah, the Most Compassionate Provider, gives each one what fits it.

questions.question: How are the eye, ear, heart, imagination, and intellect described?
questions.answer: They are described like keys that open treasures of Allah’s mercy.

questions.question: What is one example given to show how one human ability receives its special provision?
questions.answer: The eye is given the beauty and loveliness found in the world, as if it opens a treasure full of precious things.

questions.question: According to the passage, what helps all these human abilities benefit in the right way?
questions.answer: Faith helps them benefit properly.

questions.question: Why is the second form of provision called figurative rather than true natural provision?
questions.answer: Because it only seems necessary after people get used to it through bad habits and extra desires, not because life truly depends on it.

questions.question: What are the causes named for this second form of provision?
questions.answer: Habit, overuse, and using blessings in the wrong way.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about Allah’s giving of this second form?
questions.answer: It comes from His kindness, not from a fixed promise, so sometimes it is given and sometimes it is not.

questions.question: What three qualities make a person fortunate in dealing with provision?
questions.answer: Being careful with spending, being satisfied with what Allah gives, and earning in a lawful way.

questions.question: Why can lawful effort be counted as worship in this passage?
questions.answer: Because when it is done with the right intention and honesty, it becomes a kind of active asking from Allah.

questions.question: What two bad character traits are connected with misery in the passage?
questions.answer: Wastefulness and greed.

questions.question: What lesson does the passage give about laziness and wrongdoing?
questions.answer: They do not bring a good life; they lead to harm, sadness, and loss.

questions.question: What comparison is made between the stomach and other human abilities?
questions.answer: Just as the stomach needs food, the other abilities also need fitting nourishment.

questions.question: How does the passage show that each human ability has its own special nourishment?
questions.answer: It says each one is given a suitable share from Allah’s mercy that brings it joy in its own way.

questions.question: What is the main message of the example about the eye?
questions.answer: The world’s beauty is like a special gift for seeing, and the eye is made to receive that gift.

questions.question: Which kind of provision in the passage is connected to habits that can fool people into thinking something extra is necessary?
questions.answer: The second kind of provision is connected to those habits.

questions.question: What makes a person “happy” in the passage’s teaching about provision?
questions.answer: Living with moderation, contentment, halal effort, thankfulness, and acceptance of Allah’s gifts.

questions.question: What does the passage say a person should think about frugality?
questions.answer: A person should see it as something beneficial and even joyful, not as a burden.

questions.question: How does the passage connect contentment with worship?
questions.answer: It teaches that being content and striving lawfully can count as worship when done for Allah.

questions.question: What picture is given of a person ruined by greed?
questions.answer: He runs after many ways to gain more, gives up proper effort, lives poorly, and harms himself.

questions.question: What does the passage mean by saying a person can “put his own life to death”?
questions.answer: It means he destroys the goodness and peace of his own life through bad choices.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about the human heart, spirit, and mind?
questions.answer: They all need their own kind of nourishment just as the body does.

questions.question: From where does this non-physical nourishment come?
questions.answer: It comes from Allah’s mercy.

questions.question: Why are human abilities compared to keys?
questions.answer: Because they open the way to receive special gifts and signs from Allah’s mercy.

questions.question: How does faith help a person use these “keys” well?
questions.answer: Faith helps the person understand and enjoy Allah’s gifts in the right way.

questions.question: What false idea about needs is corrected in the beginning of the passage?
questions.answer: The passage corrects the idea that every wanted thing is a real necessity.

questions.question: Why is the second form of provision not secure in the same way as true needs?
questions.answer: Because it is based on extra wants shaped by habit, not on what is truly required for life.

questions.question: What does the passage teach a believer to do instead of being wasteful?
questions.answer: A believer should be careful with blessings, stay content, and seek provision through lawful work.

questions.question: How can earning a living become a kind of prayer?
questions.answer: When a person works honestly and depends on Allah, the effort itself becomes a practical request for provision.

questions.question: What attitude should a believer have toward Allah’s blessings?
questions.answer: A believer should receive them with gratitude and appreciation.

questions.question: Which behaviors are linked with a miserable life?
questions.answer: Extravagance, greed, laziness, wrongdoing, and chasing after people for more.

questions.question: What important comparison does the passage make to explain spiritual and mental needs?
questions.answer: It compares the body’s need for food with the inner self’s need for its own nourishment.

questions.question: Name three human faculties in the passage that receive their own kind of provision.
questions.answer: The heart, the eye, and the intellect.

questions.question: What does it mean that each faculty receives provision in a fitting form?
questions.answer: It means Allah gives each one what matches its purpose and nature.

questions.question: Why is the eye mentioned as an example?
questions.answer: It helps show clearly that one ability can enjoy a special gift, such as the beauty spread throughout the world.

questions.question: What do all the faculties mentioned have in common?
questions.answer: They all are made to receive mercy from Allah and benefit through iman.

questions.question: In the passage, what turns some extra things into something people wrongly feel they must have?
questions.answer: Repeated habits, wasteful living, and wrong use make them seem necessary.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about relying on Allah while seeking provision?
questions.answer: A person should seek provision in lawful ways while trusting Allah and being satisfied with what He gives.

questions.question: Why is frugality described in a positive way?
questions.answer: Because it protects a person from loss and helps bring peace and happiness.

questions.question: What is the connection between greed and suffering in the passage?
questions.answer: Greed pushes a person into wrong choices and leaves him unhappy and troubled.

questions.question: According to the passage, what kind of striving should never be left?
questions.answer: Halal striving should not be left.

questions.question: What does the passage suggest about a life spent chasing worldly gain everywhere?
questions.answer: It is a low and unhappy way to live.

questions.question: What broader meaning of “provision” is taught after the part about food and money?
questions.answer: Provision also includes what the soul, heart, mind, and senses need.

questions.question: What do the eye and ear show us about human beings?
questions.answer: They show that people are created with different abilities, and each ability has its own gift from Allah.

questions.question: How does the passage describe Allah’s giving to these abilities?
questions.answer: It describes His giving as generous, joyful, and perfectly suited to each one.

questions.question: What treasure does the eye open, according to the example?
questions.answer: It opens the wonders and beauties spread across the universe.

questions.question: What is the role of faith in enjoying the gifts given to human faculties?
questions.answer: Faith lets a person benefit from them properly and understand them as blessings from Allah.

questions.question: What are the two main topics covered in this target passage?
questions.answer: First, it explains the second kind of provision and the right and wrong ways to seek it. Second, it explains that human inner faculties also receive their own provision from Allah.

questions.question: What is the source of the second kind of provision if it is given?
questions.answer: It comes from Allah’s generosity.

questions.question: Why might this second kind of provision not be given?
questions.answer: Because it is not something guaranteed like a true life need.

questions.question: How should a Muslim respond when Allah gives blessings beyond basic needs?
questions.answer: A Muslim should accept them thankfully and use them with appreciation.

questions.question: What makes lawful effort special in this passage?
questions.answer: It is treated like an act of worship and a deed that asks Allah for rizq.

questions.question: What opposite path leads to misery?
questions.answer: The path of excess, greed, laziness, and unfair behavior leads to misery.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about the needs of the human being as a whole?
questions.answer: A human being has both physical needs and inner needs.

questions.question: Which inner parts are named as needing provision?
questions.answer: The heart, spirit, intelligence, eye, ear, and mouth are named.

questions.question: How is Allah’s mercy shown toward these different parts?
questions.answer: He gives each one a special kind of nourishment that suits it and brings it delight.

questions.question: Why are human faculties said to be like keys to mercy?
questions.answer: Because they help a person reach and receive different blessings placed in creation.

questions.question: What can we infer about faith from the ending of the target passage?
questions.answer: Faith helps a person use all these gifts correctly and gain more benefit from them.
